Monzo has a lot to offer in terms of a quality app, which let’s face it is very good. They use the app to offer innovative products, and range of services. However their service quality is lacking, without the history of an established bank they quickly fall short in how they handle customers finances and their products whilst advertised and marketed well, are not good financial decisions and in some cases such as Flex can harm customers.

Their bank accounts and fees are ok for most and would appeal to the younger customers due to their apps etc, however they offer poor value on the paid accounts with little actual useful benefit beyond a different card design. They also have tendency to obscure or hide information in an effort to make things like loans or cards easier and quicker to apply for at the expense of customers being fully informed. This lack of clarity could harm customers as the ease of applying for products or services may lead them to make financial decisions not in their best interests. 

Flex is a good example of this, easy and quick to apply for an marketed as a credit card. However this is quite blatantly mis-selling as they are quick to tell you it isn’t a credit card the second you want to do something like a balance transfer. Flex should you end up paying interest is insanely expensive and a really bad product to use that many customers may end up using purely because it was easy and appeared simple so they didn’t do the research. Monzo know this and deliberately take advantage by defaulting to interest paying periods, offering high limits, and misleading customers. They similarly do the same with loans where the ease of applying and relative lack of upfront clarity means customers may not think to look elsewhere.

Monzo is an ok bank, but don’t use anything beyond the basic account. If you want actual banking then look elsewhere for an established bank that is not driven entirely by marketing and fancy apps. 

I would summarise by saying that Monzo simply cannot be trusted to do what’s best for their customers and is more interested in treading a fine line between the bare minimum required by regulators and outright mis-selling of financial services. Personally I’d look elsewhere.

There are several issues preventing me from doing so: low ATM withdrawal limits (especially for a bank that used to bill itself as a travel card), extra features that require Monzo Premium which in my opinion are part of the offering of their competitors as standard, but the main reason I could never trust them with my money is their poor customer support.

I am currently trying to resolve an issue involving a £150 overseas cash withdrawal, wherein I was charged by the ATM but no cash came out. I have followed their Help section directions, but unfortunately am unable to dispute the transaction, as the Help section directs me towards headings that do not exist for this transaction. The Monzo customer support staff are equally useless. I have been bounced between 4 representatives so far, each of whom will only send me a template message telling me to follow the directions of the Help section. When I raise the issue that I can’t follow the Help section, guess what? I am bounced to the next representative. It is becoming frustrating, as I obviously need that £150 back. 

The Help section is confusingly laid out, and the processes to begin transactions disputes are obscure to the point of being suspicious. Whether it is incompetent app design or an intentional ploy to dissuade customers from disputing payments, it is enough for me to no longer recommend this bank either for travel or (definitely not) for main account use. I have increasingly been using their competitors such as Starling, which I think offer a similar service with fewer of these issues. When my dispute is eventually resolved, it is likely I will transition away from Monzo completely. No, it would appear that my usage (this is not my primary CA and does not receive my salary) is not the sort of business Monzo want. 

It’s pretty short-sighted though. Monzo have seen me as not being DIRECTLY profitable but have failed to realise that:
~ As a strong advocate I have recommended Monzo to two colleagues who opened accounts, and my uni student daughter who DOES use it as her primary current account and would ordinarily be a long term customer. 
~ As a director of a limited company I was considering moving my business account from barclays to Monzo
~ I have been cross sold bonds and savings accounts, and would consider other product offerings if they were available

But no, the brief love affair is over and Monzo have fallen significantly from grace, a fall that I will recount to those I recommended Monzo to, and others if the topic arises. Pity really, but they’re not the only neobank in town so will give one of the others a blast

I have now been using Monzo for 9 months solid with absolutely no issues. Opened an account in less than 5 minutes. Card arrived less than 48 hours laters. Registered it to my account in 2 minutes flat. Been trouble free. No silly forms. No mother’s maiden names etc etc etc

The card itself is a cut above the average “boring” looking debit card. The app is nothing short of fantastic. It’s easy to navigate, gives you a good overview of your finances plus the round up feature is always welcome. You can split your money into multiple “pots” but still view it all in the same place. The app also gives your phone a little “cha ching” noise every time you spend or receive money. Good for keeping track of your comings and goings. They offer savings via partner banks which are all visible and manageable via the app. The current account is so good, that my partner decided to open one and has had an identical experience. Top notch and hassle free. 

Adding, paying and transferring money is literally 4-5 taps. It’s even easier if the money’s is going to another Monzo account. There’s a feature that allows you to “sync” (much like Bluetooth) and find nearby Monzo users that are also using the sync function at that moment. Both agree to the transaction and the money is transferred. No more messing about with account numbers and sort codes bla bla bla. 

The only downside is the depositing and withdrawing of physical cash. Easy to work around if Monzo is your main account and your salary is paid straight in. Or, like myself, you just transfer the money to Monzo from another current account. However, if you’re self employed and tend to do a lot of cash work, it could become a problem as you can only deposit and withdraw a certain amount of physical cash a month. To clarify: you can digitally (via the app) add or withdraw as much money as you like from a Monzo current account. But there are limits on physical cash deposits and withdrawals. On the bright side you can deposit cash via any paypoint (which are at almost every small shop across the country eg Co-Op), but only a few hundred quid a month. Same for ATM withdrawals.

One last foot note on Monzos customer service: It’s pretty good. They have a feature like a live chat where you basically type your message then the app notifies you (like a typical text message message notification) when it’s been replied to so you can literally text a human about any issues or queries you have. Useful for a 90s child like myself who grew with the information era. This may not suit some of the older crowd but there are alternative communication mediums.

In summary: If you are looking to dip your toes into the the digital banking world and want something UK based and user friendly, Monzo is the bank for you. Starling and Revolut offer better incentives when travelling abroad, but your average bloke doesn’t sod off on the jet set every other month. Plus Monzos app is a bit more forward and more easily manageable. My advice would be look at all three challenger banks and find the one that is best suited to you. For me it’s Monzo

Having used Monzo for four years, I have never had a problem and would recommend this to anyone that’s not technophobic. 

Monzo provides you transparency for your money. I struggled with savings accounts for years because I couldn’t draw the line between what was a house deposit or what I was saving for a holiday for example, so I started using Monzo primarily for the pots feature. Being able to split up my money without making new accounts is so helpful and I’ve definitely become a better saver for this. 

Over time I’ve started to use Monzo for more and more. At first, I used it for my every day spending, because my available balance was immediately updated to reflect what I spent. I’ve noticed my other accounts have followed with this type of real-time update, and this shows how Monzo is at the forefront of customer-first features, leaving the high street branches desperately trying to catch up. 

Monzo provides notifications when direct debits are going to be higher or lower than expected. Being able to rely on Monzo to provide information like this means I don’t have to monitor these transactions as often. 

Monzo interacts with its customer base on a regular basis, and feature ideas come from what users request rather than what some executive thinks would looks good. Pots have recently had an update, where they can be reordered or hidden. This iterative development shows that Monzo will have the capacity to put real customer needs first. 

Lots of these one-star reviews are in relation to accounts being frozen. Monzo have been entirely transparent about the fact accounts get frozen, and this is follow financial regulations. The allegations that Monzo “stole” money are sensationalised statements - users cannot get access to money from frozen accounts, but accounts are either unfrozen or closed, with money being returned to the source. Please take such reviews with a pinch of salt, they will be part of an understandably emotional response. Accounts are frozen with every bank, this is not a reflection of Monzo. 

Monzo have grown incredibly quickly, and we as users now have to give them the space they need to adapt their processes and infrastructure to keep up with us. 

Keep up the good work, Monzo. Customer focused challenger banks are the future.

Overall the app is really good. However I think it would be made excellent with a few added features. 

Some of the good points:

-Salary sort and savings pots are great, and I think the option to split your salary into spending, saving and bills is a fantastic feature. 

-It takes into account all upcoming recurring bills/expenses and subtracts the amount from your available spending so you don’t go over, and gives you a forecast based on your spending habits.

-Being able to set monthly spend budgets by category is a good idea 

Some of the things I’d like to see added to the app in future:

-Incoming money doesn’t subtract from spending:
For this one it’s a little bit picky but in my opinion it’s a big deal. If you go halves on let’s say a dominos with your mum, you pay on your Monzo card and she transfers you some money from her (nationwide) account for example. Even if you set the incoming money to the same category as what went out, it still says you spent the whole amount on your monthly spending, which makes it look like you’ve spent more than you actually have. Starling Bank is really good for this feature.

-Spending percentages: Again picky but I’d quite like to know that 36% of my overall spending went into my motorbike fuel tank. A feature that Starling again does well.

-UI: It just seems a little bit.. simple. It’s just there. It doesn’t look particularly nice, it just does the job, which I suppose is good but a nice UI really makes or breaks an app. Take a look at Starling UI and you’ll know what I mean. (Sounds like I’m fanboying Starling but Starling and Monzo can trade blows I assure you, and you need to compare directly with the competition).

Overall it’s a great app, but with a few little improvements (UI please), it could be unstoppable, way ahead of the competition. I’m continuing to trial the app and am considering switching from Starling to Monzo permanently but at the moment I’m going to stick with my current bank.

I wanted to write a really positive review for Monzo but my early impression is very mixed.

The app is also brilliant and offers lots of features that the big banks don’t offer such as the ability to freeze your card, track your spending habits, set spending limits. However, the Touch ID log-in feature doesn’t work. Every time I activate this feature via the app, it automatically switches off when I log out. This means that I have to login in via a link to my email account. This is messy and involves requesting an email, clicking on the link and then opening up the app, I also don’t think this is anything like as secure as using Touch ID.

I emailed the Monzo help desk to see if I was doing something wrong and nearly 3 weeks later I haven’t had a response. This morning I tried phoning the help desk and after 10 minutes holding the line I was told via the automated system that there was no one available to speak to me and to call back another time.

I understand Monzo is a fintech start up business and the business model doesn’t involve having hundreds of staff answering the phone, but there needs to be some sort of customer service for when things aren’t working such as my Touch ID.

I hope I’ll get this sorted soon, Monzo have a brilliant app and it’s definitely the future of banking, but they do have some teething problems to sort out first.

Monzo is a really innovative banking company and their app is excellent in this respect. Their services are still in Beta and so of course there are restrictions regarding the pre-paid card, but it's clear for anyone considering the long-term impact, Monzo will really shake up the banking industry.  The current verson of the app allows you to manage your pre-paid card (used whilst the company awaits the removal of the restrictions on their banking license), view/categorise/annotate your transactions, get incredibly quick support (I've had responses in 5 minutes from employees), top-up and more. It can only improve from here, and so far the features such as the push notifications and intelligent purchase data retrieval (location of store, type of purchase etc) is really impressive and certainly not something I've seen with any other bank.  It would appear a lot of other reviewers don't understand Monzo particularly well, and that's fine - the bank isn't for everyone and is still in testing. I feel that the reviews section deserves unbiased opinions from those who value technical innovation though, and the above is just my two cents. I highly recommend Monzo.
